summary: Focused backend auth verification for the admin login accessibility bug fix. All 9 tests passed. Both the canonical admin email (admin@fotuber.com.tr) and the newly seeded alias (admin@fotuber.com) authenticate successfully with FTB.2024 and return role=admin with a valid JWT. Wrong password and non-existent email return 401 with the expected Turkish message. Whitespace tolerance and case-insensitivity of the email field are working. /api/auth/me returns the correct user for both variants.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is >1700 lines — consider splitting into routers (auth, appointments, gallery, transactions) for maintainability.
Alias-admin seed logic could be extracted into a helper (seed_admin(email, password)) to remove duplication between the main and alias branches (lines 380-417).
Login endpoint returns identical 401 messages for wrong password and missing user (good for security). Keep as-is.
test_credentials: Admin main: admin@fotuber.com.tr / FTB.2024 — Admin alias: admin@fotuber.com / FTB.2024 (both work, both role=admin)
seed_data_creation: None. Alias admin is auto-seeded by on_startup in server.py.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Auth bug fix verified end-to-end at HTTPS public URL. The alias admin@fotuber.com is created/updated on backend startup with the same FTB.2024 password and role=admin. Both emails share the password but map to different user IDs (each has its own record in db.users). If future refactor removes the alias branch (server.py lines 398-417), the alias login will break — retest this file.
rca of the issue: Original bug: user tried admin@fotuber.com but seeded admin email is admin@fotuber.com.tr. Fix: on_startup now also upserts a second user document with email=admin@fotuber.com, same password hash, role=admin. Additionally the login endpoint already applies .strip().lower() to the incoming email, giving whitespace/case tolerance. Verified with 9 assertions covering both success and failure paths.
